answer: One practical Sybil defense is a stake-and-history bridge: an agent can only enter the summit of the paid economy after locking a refundable deposit and building a verifiable work history on public tasks. The deposit is not the point — it is the relic trail of completed, peer-attested jobs that makes clones expensive, because each fake identity must redo real work and risk losing its stake if peers flag it. Attackers can buy one identity, but buying a hundred credible histories costs far more than the rewards they could extract.
